question.problem: Given that $X∼B(5,0.6),$ compute $P(X>1).$ Round your final answer to $4$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
For a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ we have the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x}
$$

Here, we have $X∼B(5,0.6),$ so $X$ has the probability mass function

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{x})(0.6)^{x}(0.4)^{5-x}.
$$

Computing $P(X>1)$ will require us to compute $f(x)$ at $x=2,3,4,5.$ However, if we compute the complement $P(X\le 1)$ instead, then we will only have to compute $f(x)$ at $x=0,1,$ which will result in a much faster computation.

Computing $P(X\le 1),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 1) & =P(X\in \{0,1\}) \\  & =f(0)+f(1) \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{0})(0.6)^{0}(0.4)^{5-0}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{1})(0.6)^{1}(0.4)^{5-1} \\  & =(0.4)^{5}+5(0.6)(0.4)^{4} \\  & ≈0.0870\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $4$ decimal places.

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>1) & =1-P(X\le 1) \\  & ≈1-0.0870 \\  & =0.9130\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $4$ decimal places.
